For this reason it does not seem likely that they left to Jeremias the ark and the altar of incense, which were of the purest gold, as we have it in Exodus[[Ex 25:11||]][[Ex 30:3||]] [the second margin reference reads “xix, 3”; Ex 30:3, the gilding of the altar of incense, is meant]. Therefore, because of these things and the others said above about the death of Antiochus and the time of Demetrius, which can scarcely be reconciled with other places of Scripture, and only with great difficulty, as is clear from what has been said above, this second book, and above all as regards its preface, is reckoned by many to be quite apocryphal. This, however, I leave to the judgement of my elders. Thus far Lyra.

paras.t: Circa hæc recolo quæ Magister in historiis recitat, S. Epiphanium episcopum de Jeremia dixisse: Hic est Jeremias, qui templum evertendum prænoscens, arcam testamenti cum his quæ in ea erant, tulit, et precibus suis eam absorberi fecit in petra. Petram vero digito signans, nomen Dei impressit, scilicet tetragrammaton, ut dicitur. Et factum est sigillum in similitudinem sculpturæ, quæ ferro cavatur; ipsumque Dei nomen operimento nubis celatum est, ut ex tunc nec locum quis recognoscere queat, nec ipsum legere nomen usque in diem hunc et usque in finem. Et instar pristinæ figuræ, illic sæpe nubes, vel ignis nocturno fit tempore, eo quod gloria Dei ab ejus lege non desinat. Est autem petra illa in eremi terra inter duos montes, in quibus jacent Moyses et Aaron. Dixitque Jeremias præsentibus: Dominus de Sion recessit ad cælos, inde rursus in virtute venturus; et erit signum præsentiæ ejus, quando universæ gentes adoraverint lignum. Dixitque: Hanc arcam præter Aaron producere nemo poterit; et tabulas quæ in ea sunt, nullus aperiet sacerdotum, nisi electus Dei Moyses. Et in prima resurrectione resurget hæc arca, et exibit de petra, atque ponetur in monte Sina, et omnes gentes congregabuntur ad eam, regressum Dei sustinentes, et adversarium qui eos quæsiturus est interimere fugientes. Hæc Epiphanius, cujus verba in aliquibus videntur dissonare a verbis litteræ hujus. Suntque verba illa Epiphanii ad intelligendum difficilia, sicut et textus iste.
paras.en: On these matters I recall what the Master relates in the Histories [that is, Peter Comestor, in his *Historia scholastica*], that St. Epiphanius the bishop said of Jeremias: This is Jeremias, who, foreknowing that the temple was to be overthrown, took the ark of the testament with the things that were in it, and by his prayers caused it to be swallowed up in a rock. And marking the rock with his finger, he imprinted on it the name of God, namely the tetragrammaton [the four-lettered name of God], as is said. And it became a seal like a carving that is hollowed out with iron; and the very name of God was hidden by a covering of cloud, so that from then on no one can recognize the place, nor read the name itself, until this day and until the end. And after the likeness of the former figure, a cloud is often there, or a fire by night, because the glory of God does not depart from his law. Now that rock is in the land of the desert, between two mountains in which Moses and Aaron lie. And Jeremias said to those present: The Lord has withdrawn from Sion to the heavens, and will come thence again in power; and this shall be the sign of his presence, when all the nations shall have adored the wood [that is, the wood of the Cross]. And he said: No one shall be able to bring forth this ark but Aaron; and none of the priests shall open the tables that are in it, except Moses, the chosen one of God. And in the first resurrection this ark shall rise again, and shall come out of the rock, and shall be set on mount Sina [the margin gives the other reading “Sion”], and all the nations shall be gathered to it, waiting for the return of God, and fleeing the adversary who will seek to destroy them. Thus far Epiphanius, whose words seem in some points to disagree with the words of the text here. And those words of Epiphanius are hard to understand, as is this text also.

paras.t: Certum est tamen, litteram istam, si salvari debeat, non ita esse intelligendam, quod in primo regis Messiæ adventu fuerint tabernaculum Moysis, arca et altare incensi, realiter ac corporaliter ostendenda. Spiritualiter vero, et quantum ad res significatas per ea, ostensa sunt in primo Christi adventu, et deinceps. Quando autem et qualiter ostendenda sint realiter ac corporaliter, non scio, nec definire præsumo; tamen ut tetigi, littera ista a falsitate poterit per piam et mysticam expositionem aliquam excusari. Quum enim ab Ecclesia receptus sit liber iste ad legendum publice in divino Officio, non apparet tutum quod dicatur falsus sive apocryphus: quia, ut sanctus ait Hieronymus, apocrypha nescit Ecclesia.
paras.en: It is certain, however, that this text, if it is to be upheld, is not to be understood as if the tabernacle of Moses, the ark and the altar of incense were to be shown really and bodily at the first coming of the King Messias. But spiritually, and as regards the things signified by them, they were shown at the first coming of Christ, and from then on. When and how they are to be shown really and bodily, I do not know, nor do I presume to define; yet, as I have touched on, this text can be cleared of falsehood by some godly and mystical exposition. For since this book has been received by the Church to be read publicly in the divine Office, it does not appear safe to call it false or apocryphal: for, as St. Jerome says, the Church knows nothing of apocrypha.

paras.t: Porro, quod in præmemoratis verbis Nicolai de Lyra habetur, arcam et altare incensi fuisse de auro purissimo, non potest stare secundum quod sonat. Arca namque fuit de lignis setim, ut legitur in Exodo. Fuerat vero deaurata intus et extra auro mundissimo, ut eodem patet capitulo. Altare quoque incensi fuit de lignis setim, secundum illud Exodi, Facies et altare ad adolendum thymiama de lignis setim; quod etiam fuerat deauratum, ut fertur ibidem. Insuper, quod in præhabitis Epiphanii verbis asseritur, quod petra illa est in eremi terra inter duos montes, in quibus jacent Moyses et Aaron, requirit intelligentiam piam. De Aaron equidem constat, quod in monte Hor sit sepultus, ut in Numeris recitatur. Moysen vero non in monte, sed in valle esse sepultum, probatur per id Deuteronomii ultimo: Mortuus est Moyses servus Domini in terra Moab jubente Domino, et sepelivit eum in valle terræ Moab.
paras.en: Further, what is found in the words of Nicholas of Lyra quoted above, that the ark and the altar of incense were of the purest gold, cannot stand as it sounds. For the ark was of setim wood, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 25:10||]]; but it had been overlaid within and without with the purest gold, as is clear from the same chapter[[Ex 25:11||]]. The altar of incense, too, was of setim wood, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 30:1|Thou shalt make also an altar to burn incense, of setim wood|Facies et altare ad adolendum thymiama de lignis setim]]; and it too had been overlaid with gold, as is recorded in the same place[[Ex 30:3||]]. Moreover, what is asserted in the words of Epiphanius given above, that that rock is in the land of the desert, between two mountains in which Moses and Aaron lie, calls for a godly understanding. For of Aaron indeed it is certain that he was buried on mount Hor, as is related in Numbers[[Num 20:25||]][[Num 20:29||]]. But that Moses was buried not on a mountain but in a valley is proved by this, in the last chapter of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 34:5|And Moses the servant of the Lord died there, in the land of Moab, by the commandment of the Lord|Mortuus est Moyses servus Domini in terra Moab jubente Domino]], [[Deut 34:6|And he buried him in the valley of the land of Moab|et sepelivit eum in valle terræ Moab]].

paras.t: Consequenter ad celebrationem Purificationis Dedicationisque templi, inducuntur facta Salomonis ac Moysis. Et sicut quum Salomon petiit ut locus sanctificaretur magno Deo: id est, Salomon exoravit ut templum a se ædificatum, consecraretur et acceptabile esset Deo immenso, ut tertio Regum describitur, secundo quoque Paralipomenon; manifestabat hæc. Magnifice enim sapientiam tractabat, id est, Salomon sapientiam sibi infusam, præclare ostendit in templi constructione et dedicatione, imo in increatæ Sapientiæ honoratione ac cultu; et ut sapientiam habens, obtulit sacrificium dedicationis et consummationis templi: juxta illud tertii Regum: Rex et omnis Israel cum eo, immolabant victimas coram Domino; et dedicaverunt templum Domini. Sicut et Moyses orabat ad Dominum, et descendit ignis de cælo aerio, et consumpsit holocaustum. Hoc fuit in consecratione Aaron filiorumque ejus, juxta illud Levitici: Egressus ignis a Domino, devoravit holocaustum, et adipes qui erant super altare. Sic et Salomon oravit, et descendit ignis de cælo, et consumpsit holocaustum, a Salomone per manus sacerdotum oblatum, secundum illud secundi Paralipomenon: Quumque complesset Salomon fundens preces, ignis descendit de cælo, et devoravit holocausta et victimas.
paras.en: Next, for the celebration of the Purification and Dedication of the temple, the deeds of Solomon and of Moses are brought in. And as [[2:8|when Solomon prayed that the place might be sanctified to the great God|quum Salomon petiit ut locus sanctificaretur magno Deo]]: that is, Solomon besought that the temple built by him might be consecrated and be acceptable to the immense God, as is described in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 8:22||]], and also in the second of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 6:14||]] [the margin gives III Reg. viii with a verse read as “32 et seq.” (Solomon's prayer begins at 3 Kings 8:22), and II Par. vi, 14 et seq.]; [[2:8|he shewed it|manifestabat hæc]]. [[2:9|For he treated wisdom in a magnificent manner|Magnifice enim sapientiam tractabat]], that is, Solomon splendidly showed forth the wisdom infused into him, in the building and dedication of the temple, nay, in the honour and worship of the uncreated Wisdom; [[2:9|and like a wise man|et ut sapientiam habens]] [literally “as having wisdom”], [[2:9|he offered the sacrifice of the dedication, and of the finishing of the temple|obtulit sacrificium dedicationis et consummationis templi]]: according to that of the third book of Kings: [[3 Kings 8:62|the king, and all Israel with him, offered victims before the Lord|Rex et omnis Israel cum eo, immolabant victimas coram Domino]]; and they [[3 Kings 8:63|dedicated the temple of the Lord|dedicaverunt templum Domini]]. [[2:10|And as Moses prayed to the Lord|Sicut et Moyses orabat ad Dominum]], [[2:10|and fire came down from heaven|et descendit ignis de cælo]], the heaven of the air, [[2:10|and consumed the holocaust|et consumpsit holocaustum]]. This was at the consecration of Aaron and his sons, according to that of Leviticus: [[Lev 9:24|a fire, coming forth from the Lord, devoured the holocaust, and the fat that was upon the altar|Egressus ignis a Domino, devoravit holocaustum, et adipes qui erant super altare]]; [[2:10|so Solomon also prayed|Sic et Salomon oravit]], [[2:10|and fire came down from heaven|et descendit ignis de cælo]], [[2:10|and consumed the holocaust|et consumpsit holocaustum]], offered by Solomon through the hands of the priests, according to that of the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 7:1|when Solomon had made an end of his prayer, fire came down from heaven, and consumed the holocausts and the victims|Quumque complesset Salomon fundens preces, ignis descendit de cælo, et devoravit holocausta et victimas]].

paras.t: Dixitque Moyses, eo quod non sit manducatum quod erat pro peccato: id est, Moyses reprehendit filios Aaron, quia non comederunt hostiam pro peccato oblatam; sed ipse Moyses invenit eam exustam. Unde in littera subditur: et consumptum est, id est igne altaris exustum, quod fuerat comedendum. Hinc scriptum est in Levitico: Inter hæc, hircum qui oblatus fuerat pro peccato quum quæreret Moyses, exustum reperit; iratusque contra filios Aaron, ait: Cur non comedistis hostiam pro peccato, etc.? Similiter et Salomon octo diebus celebravit dedicationem. Tertio libro Regum de hac fertur celebritate: Fecit ergo Salomon in tempore illo festivitatem celebrem septem diebus et septem diebus, id est quatuordecim diebus. Quomodo ergo hic dicitur celebrasse dedicationem octo diebus? Ad quod quis dicere posset, quod numerus iste non ponitur hic per præcisionem numeri majoris, et quod minor non excludit majorem. Efficacius autem respondendum per illud secundi Paralipomenon: Fecit Salomon solennitatem in tempore illo septem diebus; fecitque die octavo collectam, eo quod dedicasset altare septem diebus. Itaque de illis primis octo diebus hic agitur. Nempe, quod Salomon dicitur quatuordecim diebus celebritatem fecisse, exponitur quod primis septem diebus celebritatem fecit de templi dedicatione, aliis septem celebravit festivitatem Tabernaculorum mox sequentem.
paras.en: [[2:11|And Moses said|Dixitque Moyses]]: [[2:11|Because the sin offering was not eaten|eo quod non sit manducatum quod erat pro peccato]]: that is, Moses rebuked the sons of Aaron because they had not eaten the victim offered for sin, but Moses himself found it burnt up. Hence there follows in the text: [[2:11|it was consumed|consumptum est]], that is, what should have been eaten was burnt up by the fire of the altar. Hence it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 10:16|While these things were a doing, when Moses sought for the buck goat, that had been offered for sin, he found it burnt|Inter hæc, hircum qui oblatus fuerat pro peccato quum quæreret Moyses, exustum reperit]]; [[Lev 10:16|And being angry with|iratusque contra]] [[Lev 10:16|the sons of Aaron|filios Aaron]], [[Lev 10:16|he said|ait]]: [[Lev 10:17|Why did you not eat|Cur non comedistis]] [[Lev 10:17|the sacrifice for sin|hostiam pro peccato]], etc.? [[2:12|So Solomon also celebrated the dedication eight days|Similiter et Salomon octo diebus celebravit dedicationem]]. In the third book of Kings it is said of this celebration: [[3 Kings 8:65|And Solomon made at the same time a solemn feast|Fecit ergo Salomon in tempore illo festivitatem celebrem]] [[3 Kings 8:65|seven days and seven days, that is, fourteen days|septem diebus et septem diebus, id est quatuordecim diebus]] [the margin gives III Reg. viii, 62; the words are those of 3 Kings 8:65]. How then is he said here to have celebrated the dedication for eight days? To this one might say that this number is not put here so as to cut off the greater number [*per præcisionem*, “by way of exclusion”], and that the less does not exclude the greater. But it is answered more forcefully by that of the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 7:8|Solomon kept the solemnity at that time seven days|Fecit Salomon solennitatem in tempore illo septem diebus]]; [[2 Par 7:9|And he made on the eighth day a solemn assembly, because he had kept the dedication of the altar seven days|fecitque die octavo collectam, eo quod dedicasset altare septem diebus]]. So it is of those first eight days that this passage treats. And indeed, as to Solomon's being said to have held the celebration for fourteen days, it is explained that for the first seven days he held the celebration of the dedication of the temple, and for the other seven he celebrated the feast of Tabernacles, which followed straight after.

paras.t: Inferebantur autem in descriptionibus et commentariis Nehemiæ hæc eadem: id est, de observanda festivitate Dedicationis templi tempore Esdræ et Nehemiæ ædificati, continebantur et concludebantur similia jam prædictis in quibusdam scripturis et commentis Nehemiæ: quæ scripta non habentur, sicut nec præallegatæ descriptiones Jeremiæ prophetæ. Verumtamen in Esdra habetur de solennitate Dedicationis templi illius. Et qualiter construens, id est, ipse Nehemias faciens, bibliothecam, congregavit de regionibus libros et Prophetarum et David. Tempore enim illo congregavit Esdras veteris Testamenti volumina a Chaldæis incensa, videlicet Pentateuchum, Psalterium, Prophetarumque libros: quos sic reparatos, Nehemias de regionibus Judææ, Samariæ et Galilææ seu aliunde collegit, atque in bibliothecam suam redegit. Epistolas quoque regum Judæ memoria dignas, sic congregavit; et de donariis, id est, scripta de muneribus exhibendis seu offerendis collegit cum ceteris. Similiter autem et Judas ea quæ didicerat per bellum, quod nobis acciderat, congregavit omnia: id est, Judas Machabæus fecit conscribi ea quæ cognovit per bella quæ Judæis suo tempore contigerunt, in quibus bellis multa magna et mirabilia Dei auxilia apparuerunt, quæ æterna memoria sunt condigna. Si ergo desideratis hæc, id est, si libros istos habere optatis, mittite qui perferant vobis, id est, destinate aliquos ad nos, qui vobis eos deportent.
paras.en: [[2:13|And these same things were set down in the memoirs, and commentaries of Nehemias|Inferebantur autem in descriptionibus et commentariis Nehemiæ hæc eadem]]: that is, concerning the keeping of the feast of the Dedication of the temple built in the time of Esdras and Nehemias, things like those already said were contained and set down in certain writings and commentaries of Nehemias: which writings are not extant, any more than the descriptions of Jeremias the prophet alleged above. Yet in Esdras there is mention of the solemnity of the Dedication of that temple[[1 Esd 6:16||]] [the margin's verse is unread; the dedication is told at 1 Esd 6:16]. The text goes on: [[2:13|and how he made|Et qualiter construens]], that is, Nehemias himself making, [[2:13|a library|bibliothecam]], he [[2:13|gathered together out of the countries, the books both of the prophets, and of David|congregavit de regionibus libros et Prophetarum et David]]. For at that time Esdras gathered together the volumes of the Old Testament burnt by the Chaldeans, namely the Pentateuch, the Psalter and the books of the Prophets: and these, thus restored, Nehemias collected from the regions of Judæa, Samaria and Galilee, or from elsewhere, and brought into his library. [[2:13|the epistles of the kings|Epistolas quoque regum]] of Juda, too, that were worthy of remembrance, he gathered in the same way; [[2:13|and concerning the holy gifts|et de donariis]], that is, he collected with the rest the writings on the gifts to be presented or offered. [[2:14|And in like manner Judas also|Similiter autem et Judas]] [[2:14|gathered together all|congregavit omnia]] the things he had learned [[2:14|by the war we had|per bellum, quod nobis acciderat]] [the margin gives another reading, apparently *deciderant*, “had been lost”, as in the Vulgate, for Denis's *didicerat*]: that is, Judas Machabeus had written down the things he came to know through the wars that befell the Jews in his time, in which wars many great and wonderful helps of God appeared, which are worthy of everlasting remembrance. [[2:15|Wherefore, if you want these things|Si ergo desideratis hæc]], that is, if you wish to have these books, [[2:15|send some that may fetch them to you|mittite qui perferant vobis]], that is, send some men to us to carry them to you.

paras.t: Acturi itaque Purificationem, id est, celebraturi festum de purgatione templi et consecratione altaris factis tempore Machabæorum, scripsimus vobis, ut et vos festum hoc celebretis. Bene ergo facietis si egeritis hos dies solenniter.
paras.en: [[2:16|As we are then about to celebrate the purification|Acturi itaque Purificationem]], that is, about to celebrate the feast of the cleansing of the temple and of the consecration of the altar, carried out in the time of the Machabees, [[2:16|we have written unto you|scripsimus vobis]], so that you too may celebrate this feast; [[2:16|and you shall do well, if you keep the same days|Bene ergo facietis si egeritis hos dies]] solemnly.

paras.t: Deus autem qui liberavit populum suum frequenter, videlicet tempore Moysis et Judicum ac Regum, et nunc tempore Judæ ac fratrum ejus, dando victoriam in plurimis bellis, et reddidit hæreditatem omnibus, id est, Judæis cum Juda collectis, Judæam ac hæreditaria quæque bona restituit: quod tamen tempore Simonis magis impletum est, quando unusquisque sedit sub vite sua, et sub ficulnea sua, et coluit terram suam cum pace, ut dictum est in primo libro Machabæorum; et regnum, id est regionem patrum nostrorum, vel ducatum ac regimen. Nam Judas ac fratres ejus fuerunt duces et principes, imo et summi sacerdotes populi Judæorum: imo a tempore reversionis a Babylonica captivitate usque ad Herodem Ascalonitam, habuerunt Judæi aliquos rectores et principes de populo suo, quemadmodum in volumine Genesis Jacob testatus est: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est. Aristobulus vero, filius Joannis Hyrcani filii Simonis, primus imposuit sibi regium diadema post reditum a Babylonica captivitate, quemadmodum Josephus tertiodecimo libro Antiquitatum describit. Et sacerdotium, id est sacerdotalem dignitatem seu pontificatum, et sanctificationem, id est templum seu sacram observantiam legis; sicut promisit in lege: quia per Moysen frequenter prædixit, quod pœnitentibus et conversis Judæis redderet terram patrum suorum. Speramus quod cito nostri miserebitur, dando nobis finalem liberationem per regem Messiam, vel eruendo nos omnino a gentilium infestatione, et congregabit de sub cælo in locum sanctum, id est de diversis regnis in terram promissionis: quod et tempore Christi impletum est per congregationem spiritualem in fide, spe et caritate, et in militante Ecclesia, quemadmodum Isaiæ ultimo Dominus dixit: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mari, in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe; et adducent omnes fratres vestros.
paras.en: [[2:17|God, who hath delivered his people|Deus autem qui liberavit populum suum]] often, namely in the time of Moses and of the Judges and the Kings, and now in the time of Judas and his brethren, by giving victory in very many wars, [[2:17|and hath rendered to all the inheritance|et reddidit hæreditatem omnibus]], that is, he restored Judæa and every hereditary good to the Jews gathered with Judas: which, however, was more fully accomplished in the time of Simon, when [[1 Mach 14:12|every man sat under his vine, and under his fig tree|unusquisque sedit sub vite sua, et sub ficulnea sua]], and [[1 Mach 14:8|tilled his land with peace|coluit terram suam cum pace]], as is said in the first book of Machabees; [[2:17|and the kingdom|et regnum]], that is, the country of our fathers, or leadership and rule. For Judas and his brethren were leaders and princes, nay, even high priests of the Jewish people: indeed, from the time of the return from the Babylonian captivity until Herod of Ascalon the Jews had some rulers and princes from their own people, as Jacob testified in the book of Genesis: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est]]. Aristobulus, the son of John Hyrcanus the son of Simon, was the first after the return from the Babylonian captivity to put the royal diadem on himself, as Josephus describes in the thirteenth book of the Antiquities; [[2:17|and the priesthood|Et sacerdotium]], that is, the priestly dignity or pontificate, [[2:17|and the sanctuary|et sanctificationem]], that is, the temple, or the sacred observance of the law; [[2:18|As he promised in the law|sicut promisit in lege]]: for through Moses he often foretold that he would give back to the Jews, when they repented and turned to him, the land of their fathers[[Lev 26:41||]][[Deut 30:1||]] [the margin gives Lev. xxv(i), 41–45 and Deut. xxx, 1 et seq.]. We hope that he [[2:18|will shortly have mercy upon us|quod cito nostri miserebitur]], by giving us final deliverance through the King Messias, or by rescuing us wholly from the harassment of the Gentiles, [[2:18|and will gather us together from every land under heaven into the holy place|et congregabit de sub cælo in locum sanctum]], that is, from various kingdoms into the land of promise: which was also fulfilled in the time of Christ by a spiritual gathering in faith, hope and charity, and in the Church militant, as the Lord said in the last chapter of Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia them that draw the bow: into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mari, in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe]]; [[Is 66:20|And they shall bring all your brethren|et adducent omnes fratres vestros]].

paras.t: Consequenter auctor hujus libri tangit materiam voluminis hujus, modumque procedendi, et quid moverit eum ad compilandum hoc opus. De Juda vero Machabæo, et fratribus ejus, et de templi magni in Jerusalem sub Zorobabel facti purgatione; de quo templo Aggæus prædixit, Magna erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ, magis quam primæ; et de aræ, id est altaris, dedicatione de qua habetur in primo libro; et de illuminationibus, id est cælestibus apparitionibus, cordiumque illustrationibus, quæ de cælo factæ sunt ad eos, id est ad Judam et ejus fratres ac adjutores, qui pro Judæis fortiter fecerunt, id est, pro communi defensione Judaici populi strenue pugnaverunt, ita ut universam regionem, quum pauci essent, vindicarent, id est, injurias toti populo Judæorum illatas ab Antiocho rege ac suis ulciscerentur, quum tamen respectu adversariorum, essent perpauci, et barbaram, id est ferocem, gentilium multitudinem fugarent: ut patuit in primo libro; et civitatem Jerusalem liberarent, et leges quæ abolitæ erant, id est leges et præcepta Moysis per Antiochum quasi deleta et servari prohibita, restituerentur, id est, denuo servarentur et conscriberentur per Judam et fratres ipsius, Domino cum omni tranquillitate propitio facto illis, id est Deo eis misericorditer auxiliante.
paras.en: Next the author of this book touches on the matter of this volume, his manner of proceeding, and what moved him to compile this work. [[2:20|Now as concerning Judas Machabeus, and his brethren|De Juda vero Machabæo, et fratribus ejus]], [[2:20|and the purification of the great temple|et de templi magni]] in Jerusalem, built under Zorobabel [the margin gives the reading *purificatione*, as in the Vulgate, for the printed *purgatione*]; of which temple Aggeus foretold: [[Agg 2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|Magna erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ, magis quam primæ]]; [[2:20|and the dedication|dedicatione]] [[2:20|of the altar|et de aræ]], of which there is mention in the first book[[1 Mach 4:56||]] [the margin reads “I Mach. i, 50”; the dedication of the altar is told at 1 Mach 4:52–59]. [[2:22|And the manifestations|et de illuminationibus]], that is, heavenly apparitions and enlightenings of hearts, [[2:22|that came from heaven to them|quæ de cælo factæ sunt ad eos]], that is, to Judas and his brethren and helpers, [[2:22|that behaved themselves manfully on the behalf of the Jews|qui pro Judæis fortiter fecerunt]], that is, fought vigorously for the common defence of the Jewish people, [[2:22|so that, being but a few they made themselves masters of the whole country|ita ut universam regionem, quum pauci essent, vindicarent]] [*vindicarent*, which the Douay-Rheims renders “made themselves masters of”, Denis takes as “avenged”], that is, avenged the wrongs done to the whole people of the Jews by king Antiochus and his men, though in respect of their adversaries they were very few, [[2:22|and put to flight the barbarous|et barbaram]], that is, fierce, [[2:22|multitude|multitudinem fugarent]] of the Gentiles, as appeared in the first book[[1 Mach 4:1||]] [the margin reads “Ibid.” with a chapter numeral only partly legible, probably iv]; [[2:23|and delivered the city|et civitatem Jerusalem liberarent]] of Jerusalem, and that [[2:23|the laws that were abolished|et leges quæ abolitæ erant]], that is, the laws and precepts of Moses, as good as blotted out by Antiochus and forbidden to be kept, should be [[2:23|restored|restituerentur]], that is, kept again and written out anew by Judas and his brethren, [[2:23|the Lord with all clemency shewing mercy to them|Domino cum omni tranquillitate propitio facto illis]], that is, God mercifully helping them.

paras.t: Itemque ab Jasone Cyrenæo quinque libris comprehensa, id est diffuse conscripta in quinque codicibus, tentavimus nos uno volumine breviare. Ex hoc quidam concludunt, quod in hac compilatione plures fuerunt. Quod stare non potest: imo unus fuit breviator et auctor hujus voluminis, ut patet in fine libri hujus, quo ait: Ego quoque in his faciam finem sermonis: et si quidem bene, et ut historiæ competit, hoc et ipse velim; si autem minus digne, concedendum est mihi. Est autem consuetudo magnis authenticisque personis, dictionibus pluralis numeri uti.
paras.en: [[2:24|And all such things as have been comprised in five books by Jason, of Cyrene|Itemque ab Jasone Cyrenæo quinque libris comprehensa]], that is, written out at length in five volumes, [[2:24|we have attempted to abridge in one book|tentavimus nos uno volumine breviare]]. From this some conclude that there were several engaged in this compilation. That cannot stand: rather there was one abridger and author of this volume, as is clear at the end of this book, where he says: [[2 Mach 15:38|I also will here make an end of my narration|Ego quoque in his faciam finem sermonis]]. [[2 Mach 15:39|Which if I have done well, and as it becometh the history, it is what I desired: but if not so perfectly, it must be pardoned me|et si quidem bene, et ut historiæ competit, hoc et ipse velim; si autem minus digne, concedendum est mihi]]. Now it is the custom of great persons and persons of authority to use words of the plural number.

paras.t: Considerantes enim multitudinem librorum, et difficultatem eorum quos Jason de his rebus composuit volentibus aggredi narrationes historiarum, propter multitudinem rerum: curavimus, id est, sollicite providimus his qui volunt rerum istarum historias legere, ne tædio afficiantur ex prolixitate librorum, faciendo hunc librum compendiosum, volentibus quidem legere, ut esset animi oblectatio, id est, ut hunc librum cum cordis delectatione breviter legant; studiosis vero providimus, ut facilius possint ista memoriæ commendare; omnibus autem legentibus utilitas conferatur, id est, ut universi hæc legentes, ædificentur.
paras.en: [[2:25|For considering the multitude of books|Considerantes enim multitudinem librorum]], [[2:25|and the difficulty|et difficultatem]] of those which Jason composed on these matters, [[2:25|that they find that desire to undertake the narrations of histories, because of the multitude of the matter|volentibus aggredi narrationes historiarum, propter multitudinem rerum]]: [[2:26|We have taken care|curavimus]], that is, we have carefully provided for those who wish to read the histories of these matters, that they may not be wearied by the length of the books, by making this book a compendium: [[2:26|for those indeed that are willing to read, that it might be a pleasure of mind|volentibus quidem legere, ut esset animi oblectatio]], that is, that they may read this book in brief and with delight of heart; [[2:26|and for the studious|studiosis vero]] we have provided, [[2:26|that they may more easily commit to memory|ut facilius possint ista memoriæ commendare]] these things; [[2:26|and that all that read might receive profit|omnibus autem legentibus utilitas conferatur]], that is, that all who read these things may be edified.

paras.t: Et nobis ipsis non facilem laborem assumpsimus: quod tamen intuitu et amore communis utilitatis libenter peregimus. Propterea subditur: Sicut hi qui præparant convivium, et quærunt aliorum voluntati parere, id est obedire, parando cibaria juxta eorum velle, propter multorum gratiam, id est profectum, libenter laborem sustinemus: veritatem quidem de singulis, auctoribus concedentes, id est, credentes quod ipsi auctores librorum vera scripserunt de singulis rebus et gestis, de quibus hic loquimur: ipsi autem secundum datam, id est præconceptam et factam, formam scribendi per abbreviationem, brevitati studentes. Sicut enim novæ domus architecto de universa structura curandum est, id est, sicut principali constructori domus incumbit sollicitudo de toto ædificio et partibus ejus, et qualiter aggregentur ac redigantur in formam; ei vero qui pingere curat, id est per picturas et linitiones ornare domum jam factam, quæ apta sunt ad ornatum, exquirenda sunt, scilicet pulchri colores et confectiones, ex quibus fiunt adornationes ipsius domus: unusquisque enim habet exquirere ea, quæ ad suam pertinent artem; ita æstimandum est et in nobis, id est de nobis, qui non intendimus historicum librum originaliter compilare, sed potius descriptam historiam cum venustate abbreviare.
paras.en: [[2:27|And as to ourselves indeed|Et nobis ipsis]] [[2:27|we have taken in hand no easy task|non facilem laborem]]: which, however, we have gladly carried through, out of regard and love for the common good. Therefore there follows: [[2:28|But as they that prepare a feast, and seek to satisfy the will of others|Sicut hi qui præparant convivium, et quærunt aliorum voluntati parere]], that is, to obey it, by preparing the food according to their wish, [[2:28|for the sake of many|propter multorum gratiam]], that is, for their profit, [[2:28|we willingly undergo the labour|libenter laborem sustinemus]]: [[2:29|Leaving to the authors the exact handling of every particular|veritatem quidem de singulis, auctoribus concedentes]] [literally “granting to the authors the truth about each thing”], that is, believing that the authors of the books wrote the truth about each of the things and deeds of which we speak here; [[2:29|and as for ourselves, according to the plan proposed|ipsi autem secundum datam]], that is, the plan of writing by abridgment conceived beforehand and made, [[2:29|studying to be brief|brevitati studentes]]. [[2:30|For as the master builder of a new house must have care of the whole building|Sicut enim novæ domus architecto de universa structura curandum est]], that is, as care for the whole building and its parts, and for how they are to be put together and brought into shape, falls on the chief builder of a house; [[2:30|but he that taketh care to paint it|ei vero qui pingere curat]], that is, to adorn with paintings and coatings a house already made, [[2:30|must seek out fit things for the adorning of it|quæ apta sunt ad ornatum, exquirenda sunt]], namely fair colours and preparations, from which the adornments of the house are made: for each one has to seek out the things that belong to his own art; [[2:30|so must it be judged of us|ita æstimandum est et in nobis]], that is, concerning us, who do not intend to compile a book of history from the beginning, but rather to abridge, gracefully, a history already written.

paras.t: Denique quid historiographo competat, subditur: Etenim intellectum colligere, id est, rerum describendarum veram intelligentiam perscrutari ac adunare, et ordinare sermonem, utendo stilo convenienti ac clausulis aptis, et curiosius, id est satis diligenter, non immoderanter, partes singulas quasque disquirere, id est, investigare quascumque partes, ex quibus totum volumen est compilandum, hoc est singula quæque gesta ac verba recitatione condigna, vel singulas partes dictaminis, historiæ congruit auctori, id est historiographo. Quid autem congruat abbreviatori, subjungitur: Brevitatem vero dictionis, id est narrationis ac stili, sectari, et executiones rerum vitare, id est omittere digressiones declarantes qualiter quæque sint gesta, quando declarationes illæ non sunt utiles, brevianti concedendum est, id est, convenit ei qui scripta aliorum summatim breviare intendit.
paras.en: Lastly it is added what befits a writer of history: [[2:31|For to collect all that is to be known|Etenim intellectum colligere]], that is, to search out and bring together the true understanding of the things to be described, [[2:31|to put the discourse in order|et ordinare sermonem]], using a fitting style and apt periods, [[2:31|and curiously|et curiosius]], that is, diligently enough, not beyond measure, [[2:31|to discuss every particular point|partes singulas quasque disquirere]], that is, to investigate whatever parts the whole volume is to be compiled from, that is, each of the deeds and words worthy of being related, or the several parts of the composition, [[2:31|is the duty of the author of a history|historiæ congruit auctori]], that is, of the historiographer. And what befits an abridger is added: [[2:32|But to pursue brevity of speech|Brevitatem vero dictionis]], that is, of narrative and of style, [[2:32|and to avoid nice declarations of things|et executiones rerum vitare]], that is, to leave out digressions that explain how each thing was done, when such explanations are not useful, [[2:32|is to be granted to him that maketh an abridgment|brevianti concedendum est]], that is, it befits one who means to abridge the writings of others in summary.

paras.t: Hinc ergo, id est statim post hæc, utpote in exordio sequentis capituli, narrationem, id est exordium historiæ recitationis hujus libri, incipiemus: siquidem dicta hucusque, per modum prologi sunt inducta. Unde subjungitur: De præfatione tantum dixisse sufficiat. Stultum enim est, ante historiam effluere, id est verbis superfluis abundare, in ipsa autem historia succingi, id est nimium festinare, et sermonem abrumpere.
paras.en: [[2:33|Here then|Hinc ergo]], that is, straight after this, namely at the opening of the following chapter, [[2:33|we will begin|incipiemus]] [[2:33|the narration|narrationem]], that is, the opening of the historical account of this book: for what has been said up to here has been set down by way of a prologue. Hence there follows: [[2:33|let this be enough by way of a preface|De præfatione tantum dixisse sufficiat]]: [[2:33|for it is a foolish thing to make a long prologue|Stultum enim est, ante historiam effluere]] [literally “to overflow before the history”], that is, to abound in superfluous words, [[2:33|and to be short in the story itself|in ipsa autem historia succingi]] [literally “to be girded up”], that is, to hurry too much, and to break off the discourse.

3.title: Expositio capituli tertii: Igitur quum sancta civitas habitaretur in omni pace
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: Therefore, when the holy city was inhabited with all peace

paras.t: Præscripturus auctor libri istius victorias Judæ Machabæi et suorum, et qualiter defenderunt populum Judæorum, præmittit qualiter populus ille post magnam prosperitatem et pacem, maximas incidit clades. Itaque in isto capitulo recitat miraculosam Judæorum consolationem, et adversarii eorum prostrationem sub Onia pontifice.
paras.en: The author of this book, being about to describe the victories of Judas Machabeus and his men, and how they defended the people of the Jews, first sets down how that people, after great prosperity and peace, fell into the greatest disasters. And so in this chapter he relates the miraculous consolation of the Jews, and the overthrow of their adversary, under Onias the high priest.

paras.t: Igitur quum sancta civitas Jerusalem, ad Dei obsequium præelecta, in qua fuerunt templum et studium legis, sedes pontificis, imo et thronus regis a tempore David usque ad Sedeciam, habitaretur in omni pace, id est multum pacifice, ita quod cives ejus devoti gaudebant pace pectoris et temporis, leges etiam, id est præcepta Mosaicæ legis, adhuc optime custodirentur ab habitatoribus civitatis, propter Oniæ pontificis dispositionem et pietatem, id est ex virtuosa et exemplari præsidentia et gubernatione Oniæ, qui subditos sapienter disposuit et instruxit, atque in omni cultu Dei præcessit. Pietas quippe uno modo idem est, quod cultus Dei seu latria; alio modo sumitur pro misericordia; tertio, prout est unum de septem donis. Itaque causa bonæ conversationis civium, fuit virtuositas prælati eorum, juxta illud Ecclesiastici: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea. Unde et Salomon in Proverbiis dixit: Rex qui sedet in solio judicii, dissipat omne malum intuitu suo. Et animos odio habentes mala, id est ex bonitate cordis illorum, qui malum culpæ abhorrent: quia ad bona vere honesta seu virtuosa, sincere afficiebantur.
paras.en: [[3:1|Therefore, when the holy city|Igitur quum sancta civitas]] of Jerusalem, chosen beforehand for the service of God, in which were the temple and the study of the law, the seat of the high priest, and indeed the throne of the king from the time of David down to Sedecias, [[3:1|was inhabited with all peace|habitaretur in omni pace]], that is, very peaceably, so that its devout citizens rejoiced in peace of heart and of the times; [[3:1|and the laws|leges etiam]], that is, the precepts of the law of Moses, [[3:1|as yet were very well kept|adhuc optime custodirentur]] by the dwellers in the city, [[3:1|because of the godliness of Onias, the high priest|propter Oniæ pontificis dispositionem et pietatem]] [Denis's text reads 'because of the ordering and godliness of Onias'], that is, because of the virtuous and exemplary presiding and governing of Onias, who ordered and instructed his subjects wisely, and went before them in all the worship of God. For *godliness* in one sense is the same as the worship of God, or latria [the worship due to God alone]; in another sense it is taken for mercy; in a third, as it is one of the seven gifts[[Is 11:2||]] [the Latin *pietas* bears all three senses: worship, pity, and the gift of piety]. So the cause of the citizens' good way of life was the virtue of their prelate, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea]]. Whence Solomon also said in Proverbs: [[Prov 20:8|The king, that sitteth on the throne of judgment, scattereth away all evil with his look|Rex qui sedet in solio judicii, dissipat omne malum intuitu suo]]. And again, because of [[3:1|the hatred his soul had of evil|animos odio habentes mala]], that is, because of the goodness of heart of those who abhor the evil of sin: for they were sincerely drawn to goods that are truly honourable or virtuous [Denis takes the words, literally 'minds hating evils', of the citizens].

paras.t: Fiebat ut et ipsi reges et principes gentiles locum, id est urbem et templum Jerusalem, summo, id est valde magno, honore dignum ducerent, tanquam summi Dei habitaculum et cultus divini mansionem electam, et templum maximis muneribus illustrarent, mittendo oblationes et dona copiosa ac pretiosa ad templum, sicut et Darius rex et alii quidam in Esdra et Nehemia fecisse leguntur: quia isti gentiles, quamvis et idola colerent, tamen unius veri et summi Dei aliqualem habuerunt notitiam; ita ut Seleucus Asiæ rex, filius Antiochi Magni, de reditibus suis præstaret omnes sumptus ad ministerium sacrificiorum pertinentes. Verumtamen sicut in Scholastica fertur historia, Seleucus iste fuit iners et pessimus. Josephus vero refert patrem ejus Antiochum Magnum, fuisse liberalem ad exhibendum necessaria pro sacrificiis offerendis. Sicque Seleucus iste ad tempus in hoc imitatus videtur fuisse patrem suum, et postea pejoratus.
paras.en: [[3:2|It came to pass that even the kings themselves and the princes|Fiebat ut et ipsi reges et principes]] of the gentiles esteemed [[3:2|the place|locum]], that is, the city and temple of Jerusalem, worthy of [[3:2|the highest|summo]], that is, very great, [[3:2|honour|honore]], as the dwelling of the most high God and the chosen abode of divine worship, [[3:2|and glorified the temple with very great gifts|et templum maximis muneribus illustrarent]], by sending plentiful and precious offerings and gifts to the temple, as King Darius and certain others are read to have done in Esdras[[1 Esd 6:8||]][[1 Esd 7:15||]] and Nehemias[[2 Esd 2:8||]] [the margin's numerals are partly unreadable: it seems to give 1 Esdr. vi, 8–9; vii, 15–23; viii, 35 (perhaps 25, the king's gifts) and 2 Esdr. ii, with the verse unclear]: for these gentiles, although they also worshipped idols, yet had some sort of knowledge of the one true and most high God; so [[3:3|that Seleucus, king of Asia|ut Seleucus Asiæ rex]], the son of Antiochus the Great, [[3:3|allowed out of his revenues all the charges belonging to the ministry of the sacrifices|de reditibus suis præstaret omnes sumptus ad ministerium sacrificiorum pertinentes]]. Yet, as is told in the Scholastic History [the *Historia scholastica* of Peter Comestor], this Seleucus was idle and most wicked. But Josephus relates that his father, Antiochus the Great, was generous in providing what was needed for offering the sacrifices. And so this Seleucus seems for a time to have imitated his father in this, and afterwards to have grown worse.

paras.t: Deinde recitatur qualiter tribulatio cœpit in Jerusalem exoriri. Simon autem de tribu Benjamin, præpositus templi constitutus ad disponendum negotia templi in exterioribus rebus: non enim fuit pontifex vel sacerdos, quum fuerit de Benjamin tribu; contendebat, obsistente sibi principe sacerdotum Onia, iniquum aliquid in civitate Jerusalem moliri, id est fabricare. Invidebat namque Oniæ pontifici, voluitque plebem ad rebellionem inducere contra illum. Impii enim quasi mare fervens quod quiescere non potest, ut dicitur in Isaia.
paras.en: Next it is told how trouble began to arise in Jerusalem. [[3:4|But one Simon, of the tribe of Benjamin, who was appointed overseer of the temple|Simon autem de tribu Benjamin, præpositus templi constitutus]] to manage the business of the temple in outward things (for he was not a high priest or a priest, since he was of the tribe of Benjamin), [[3:4|strove in opposition to the high priest|contendebat, obsistente sibi principe sacerdotum]] Onias, [[3:4|to bring about some unjust thing in the city|iniquum aliquid in civitate Jerusalem moliri]], that is, to contrive it. For he envied Onias the high priest, and wished to lead the people into rebellion against him. For [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|Impii enim quasi mare fervens quod quiescere non potest]], as is said in Isaias.

paras.t: Sed quum vincere Oniam non posset, id est contra pontificem prævalere, quia Onias vir pius, justus et sapiens, erat populo carus, et multos habebat fautores in civitate potentes, venit ad Apollonium, unum de principibus regis Seleuci, et nuntiavit ei, pecuniis innumerabilibus plenum esse ærarium, id est locum thesaurorum, Jerosolymis. Erat autem ærarium istud locus situs juxta templum: in quo ærario reservabantur deposita notabilium personarum et sustentacula vitæ pauperum quædam. Et communes copias, id est opes illas ad rem publicam pertinentes, quæ non pertinent ad rationem sacrificiorum, id est ad emendum victimas oblationum, esse immensas, id est valde multas et magnas. Etenim quia Seleucus exhibebat sumptus pro sacrificiis, dixit Simon iste, opes illas ad sacrificia non spectare, præsupponens quod rex pertinentia ad sacrificia invite auferret.
paras.en: [[3:5|And when he could not overcome Onias|Sed quum vincere Oniam non posset]], that is, prevail against the high priest (because Onias, a godly, just and wise man, was dear to the people and had many powerful supporters in the city), [[3:5|he went to Apollonius|venit ad Apollonium]], one of the princes of King Seleucus, and [[3:6|told him, that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of immense sums of money|nuntiavit ei, pecuniis innumerabilibus plenum esse ærarium]] (the *treasury*, that is, the place of the treasures). Now this treasury was a place situated next to the temple, in which treasury were kept the deposits of persons of note and certain provisions for the life of the poor. And he said that [[3:6|the common store|Et communes copias]], that is, those riches belonging to the commonwealth, [[3:6|which did not belong to the account of the sacrifices|quæ non pertinent ad rationem sacrificiorum]], that is, to buying the victims of the offerings, [[3:6|was infinite|esse immensas]], that is, very many and great. For since Seleucus provided the expenses for the sacrifices, this Simon said that those riches did not concern the sacrifices, presupposing that the king would be unwilling to take away what belonged to the sacrifices.

paras.t: Statimque Heliodorus iter aggressus est versus Jerusalem, quia Seleucus commisit ei pecunias sibi afferre.
paras.en: [[3:8|So Heliodorus forthwith began his journey|Statimque Heliodorus iter aggressus est]] towards Jerusalem, because Seleucus had charged him to bring him the money.

paras.t: Tunc summus sacerdos Heliodoro declaravit, deposita esse hæc, id est opes illas esse ibi repositas, ad procurandum victualia viduarum et pupillorum egentium; quædam vero esse deposita Hircani Tobiæ viri valde eminentis, id est excellentis et fidelis personæ. In Nehemia autem fertur ipse Nehemias ejecisse de gazophylacio vasa Tobiæ infidelis. Decipi vero eos qui credidissent loco et templo, impossibile omnino esse, id est fieri non posse nec esse permittendum a Deo, quod hi deciperentur, id est, rebus atque depositis suis spoliarentur, qui ea commendaverant templo, cum fide quod conservarentur a Domino in ipso templo seu prope illud, quod per universum mundum, id est per multa regna mundi (ut sit hyperbolicus sermo), honoratur, id est, famosum habetur, pro sui veneratione, id est venerabilitate, et sanctitate, seu pro veneratione quæ Deo exhibetur in ipso.
paras.en: [[3:10|Then the high priest told him|Tunc summus sacerdos Heliodoro declaravit]] [the margin gives the Vulgate's word, *ostendit*, 'shewed', beside Denis's *declaravit*, 'declared'] [[3:10|that these were sums deposited|deposita esse hæc]], that is, that those riches were laid up there for procuring [[3:10|provisions for the subsistence of the widows and the fatherless|victualia viduarum et pupillorum]] in need; and that some [[3:11|belonged to Hircanus, son of Tobias, a man of great dignity|quædam vero esse deposita Hircani Tobiæ viri valde eminentis]], that is, of an excellent and faithful person. But in Nehemias it is told that Nehemias himself cast the vessels of the faithless Tobias out of the storehouse[[2 Esd 13:8||]]. [[3:12|But that to deceive them who had trusted to the place and temple|Decipi vero eos qui credidissent loco et templo]] [[3:12|was a thing which could not by any means be done|impossibile omnino esse]], that is, it could not happen, and was not to be permitted by God, that these should be deceived, that is, robbed of their goods and deposits, who had entrusted them to the temple in the faith that they would be kept by the Lord in the temple itself or near it, which [[3:12|is honoured|honoratur]], that is, is held famous, [[3:12|throughout the whole world|per universum mundum]], that is, through many kingdoms of the world (so that the speech is hyperbolical), [[3:12|for the reverence|pro sui veneratione]], that is, its venerableness, [[3:12|and holiness of it|et sanctitate]], or for the veneration that is shown to God in it.

paras.t: Sacerdotes autem ante altare cum sacerdotalibus stolis, id est vestibus, jactaverunt se, humiliando se intimo corde, et sacerdotaliter vestiti, ut sic benignius adspicerentur a Deo; et invocabant de cælo. Quare non dicit, Invocabant de terra, quum isti invocantes fuerint in terra, non in cœlo? Est igitur sensus: Invocabant, id est, auxilium sibi exhiberi implorabant de cœlo, rogantes eum qui de depositis legem, id est præceptum, posuit, ut his qui deposuerant ea, in præfato ærario, salva custodiret Deus, ne diriperentur. Porro de depositis Dominus aliqua jussit in Exodo.
paras.en: [[3:15|And the priests|Sacerdotes autem]] [[3:15|before the altar|ante altare]] [[3:15|in their priests' vestments|cum sacerdotalibus stolis]], that is, their robes, [[3:15|prostrated themselves|jactaverunt se]], humbling themselves in their inmost heart, and clad as priests, so that they might thus be looked upon more kindly by God; [[3:15|and called upon him from heaven|et invocabant de cælo]]. Why does it not say, They called from earth, since those who called were on earth, not in heaven? This, then, is the sense: *They called*, that is, they implored that help be shown them *from heaven*, asking him [[3:15|who made the law concerning things given to be kept|eum qui de depositis legem]], that is, the precept, [[3:15|that he would preserve them safe, for them that had deposited them|ut his qui deposuerant ea]] in the aforesaid treasury, namely God, lest they be plundered. Now concerning deposits the Lord gave certain commands in Exodus[[Ex 22:7||]].

paras.t: Jam vero qui videret summi sacerdotis vultum, mente vulnerabatur, id est, ex corde condoluit ei, tam miserabiliter disposito in facie, in cujus pallore ac mortiformi dispositione vehementissimus dolor et mœror ac pavor cordis apparuerunt. Quemadmodum enim cor gaudens exhilarat faciem, sic in mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus, prout Proverbiorum liber testatur.
paras.en: [[3:16|Now whosoever saw the countenance of the high priest, was wounded in heart|Jam vero qui videret summi sacerdotis vultum, mente vulnerabatur]], that is, grieved with him from the heart, he being so pitiably changed in his face, in whose pallor and deathlike look the most vehement sorrow, grief and dread of heart appeared. For as a [[Prov 15:13|glad heart maketh a cheerful countenance|cor gaudens exhilarat faciem]], so [[Prov 15:13|by grief of mind the spirit is cast down|in mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus]], as the book of Proverbs testifies[[Prov 17:22||]].

paras.t: Accinctæque mulieres ciliciis pectus, id est, asperitate vestis cilicinæ se affligentes ac humiliantes, etc. Sed et virgines quæ conclusæ erant, id est, virorum juvenumque adspectibus abstractæ, et ex virginali pudore remanentes in domo vel circa templum reclusæ, et piis operibus occupatæ, quousque maritarentur, procurrebant ad Oniam, tanquam ad patrem spiritualem, adsistentes ei per compassionem, orationem et fletum.
paras.en: [[3:19|And the women, girded with haircloth about their breasts|Accinctæque mulieres ciliciis pectus]], that is, afflicting and humbling themselves with the roughness of a garment of haircloth, etc. [[3:19|And the virgins also that were shut up|Sed et virgines quæ conclusæ erant]], that is, withdrawn from the sight of men and youths, and out of virginal modesty remaining shut up in the house or about the temple, and busy with works of piety until they should be married, [[3:19|came forth|procurrebant]] [[3:19|to Onias|ad Oniam]], as to a spiritual father, standing by him with compassion, prayer and weeping.

paras.t: Erat autem misera commixtæ multitudinis Judæorum ex personis utriusque sexus congregatorum, et magni sacerdotis Oniæ in agone, id est in laboriosa mentis angustia, constituti exspectatio: quoniam cum afflictione multiplici præstolabantur eventum finemque rei. Et hi invocabant Deum omnipotentem, ut credita sibi, id est deposita eis commissa, his qui crediderant, puta depositariis, cum omni integritate conservarentur, ut nihil de ipsis posset auferri.
paras.en: Now pitiful was the expectation [[3:21|of the mixed multitude|commixtæ multitudinis]] of the Jews, gathered from persons of both sexes, [[3:21|and of the high priest|et magni sacerdotis]] Onias, [[3:21|who was in an agony|in agone]], that is, set in toilsome anguish of mind: for with manifold affliction they were awaiting the outcome and end of the affair. [[3:22|And these indeed called upon almighty God|Et hi invocabant Deum omnipotentem]], [[3:22|to preserve the things that had been committed to them|ut credita sibi]], that is, the deposits entrusted to them, [[3:22|for those that had committed them|his qui crediderant]], namely the depositors, [[3:22|safe and sure|cum omni integritate conservarentur]], so that nothing could be taken from them.

paras.t: Heliodorus autem quod decreverat, perficiebat, id est, implere studebat. Sed spiritus Omnipotentis, id est voluntas seu animus Dei, imo Spiritus Sanctus ex Patre Filioque procedens, magnam fecit suæ virtutis evidentiam, id est, omnipotentiam suam publice demonstravit, perterrendo et dejiciendo Heliodorum et ejus satellites.
paras.en: [[3:23|But Heliodorus executed that which he had resolved on|Heliodorus autem quod decreverat, perficiebat]], that is, was bent on carrying it out. [[3:24|But the spirit of the Almighty God|Sed spiritus Omnipotentis]], that is, the will or mind of God, nay rather the Holy Ghost proceeding from the Father and the Son, [[3:24|gave a great evidence of his presence|magnam fecit suæ virtutis evidentiam]] [Denis reads *virtutis*, 'of his power', where the Vulgate has *ostensionis*, 'of his showing'], that is, showed his almighty power openly, by terrifying and casting down Heliodorus and his guards.

paras.t: Apparuit enim illis quidam equus terribilem habens sessorem. Fuitque angelus sanctus, in forma equitis metuendi apparens, qui et corpus equi illius formavit ac movit: sicut de curru et equis, quibus vectus fuit Elias in cœlum, tenetur.
paras.en: [[3:25|For there appeared to them a horse, with a terrible rider upon him|Apparuit enim illis quidam equus terribilem habens sessorem]]. And this was a holy angel, appearing in the form of a fearsome horseman, who also formed and moved the body of that horse: as is held of the chariot and horses by which Elias was carried into heaven[[4 Kings 2:11||]].

paras.t: Alii etiam apparuerunt duo juvenes, id est angeli in forma adolescentum, ad insinuandum quod angeli nunquam inveterascunt, qui circumsteterunt eum, et ex utraque parte Heliodorum flagellabant, etc. Eumque multa caligine circumfusum, id est præ timore et tormento nihil videntem, rapuerunt, id est, sacerdotes apprehenderunt, putantes quod mortuus esset, et ne ex præsentia exstincti cadaveris, præsertim perfidi hominis, sacer locus contaminaretur, qui etiam ex ingressu viventis alienigenæ contaminabatur; atque in sella gestatoria, id est sede portatoria, positum ejecerunt, id est, exportaverunt de ipso ærario.
paras.en: [[3:26|Moreover there appeared two other young men|Alii etiam apparuerunt duo juvenes]], that is, angels in the form of youths, to signify that angels never grow old, [[3:26|who stood by him, on either side, and scourged him|qui circumsteterunt eum, et ex utraque parte Heliodorum flagellabant]], etc. And, [[3:27|covered with great darkness|Eumque multa caligine circumfusum]] as he was, that is, seeing nothing for fear and torment, [[3:27|they took him up|rapuerunt]], that is, the priests laid hold of him, thinking that he was dead, and lest the holy place be defiled by the presence of a lifeless corpse, above all of a faithless man, the place that was defiled even by the entrance of a living foreigner; [[3:27|and having put him into a litter|atque in sella gestatoria]], that is, a carrying-chair, [[3:27|they carried him out|positum ejecerunt]], that is, they bore him out of the treasury itself.

paras.t: Considerans autem summus sacerdos, ne forte rex Seleucus suspicaretur malitiam aliquam ex Judæis circa Heliodorum consummatam, id est, quod aliqui ex Judæis armati, taliter tractassent, aut magica arte affligi fecissent Heliodorum a malignis spiritibus, obtulit pro salute viri, id est pro curatione Heliodori, hostiam salutarem cum oratione. Aliqui vero dicunt Heliodorum fuisse occisum et mortuum, atque Oniæ precibus suscitatum, quia habetur in textu, quod in supremo spiritu, id est in agone, erat constitutus. Nihilominus littera ista magis insinuare videtur, quod nondum exspiravit, sed letaliter exstitit vulneratus, moxque obiisset, nisi per preces Oniæ, vita, id est sanitas vitæ, fuisset ei donata.
paras.en: [[3:32|So the high priest, considering that the king|Considerans autem summus sacerdos, ne forte rex]] Seleucus [[3:32|might perhaps suspect that some mischief had been done to Heliodorus by the Jews|suspicaretur malitiam aliquam ex Judæis circa Heliodorum consummatam]], that is, that some of the Jews had handled him so with weapons, or had caused Heliodorus to be afflicted by evil spirits through magic art, [[3:32|offered|obtulit]] [[3:32|for the recovery of the man|pro salute viri]], that is, for the healing of Heliodorus, [[3:32|a sacrifice of health|hostiam salutarem]] with prayer. Some, indeed, say that Heliodorus was slain and dead, and raised up by the prayers of Onias, because it is said in the text that he [[3:31|was ready to give up the ghost|in supremo spiritu]], that is, was in his death agony. Nevertheless the letter seems rather to suggest that he had not yet expired, but was mortally wounded, and would soon have died, had not life, that is, the health of life, been granted him through the prayers of Onias.

paras.t: Heliodorus autem, hostia Deo oblata per manum sacerdotis, pro gratiarum actione quod fuit curatus, et votis magnis Deo promissis, etc., repedabat, id est remeabat, ad regem, etc.
paras.en: [[3:35|So Heliodorus, after he had offered a sacrifice to God|Heliodorus autem, hostia Deo oblata]] by the hand of the priest, in thanksgiving that he had been healed, [[3:35|and made great vows to him|et votis magnis Deo promissis]], etc., [[3:35|returned|repedabat]], that is, went back, [[3:35|to the king|ad regem]], etc.

paras.t: Eo quod in loco, id est in templo, vere sit Dei quædam virtus, id est potestas angelica locum custodiens, imo ipsemet Deus. Nam ipse qui in cælis habet habitationem, visitator et adjutor est loci illius, id est gratiosus et potens defensor, quoniam locus ille Deo exstitit consecratus, qui per effectum multiplicem visitavit eumdem.
paras.en: Because [[3:38|in that place|Eo quod in loco]], that is, in the temple, [[3:38|there is undoubtedly|vere sit]] [[3:38|a certain power of God|Dei quædam virtus]], that is, an angelic power guarding the place, nay rather God himself. [[3:39|For he that hath his dwelling in the heavens, is the visitor and protector of that place|Nam ipse qui in cælis habet habitationem, visitator et adjutor est loci illius]], that is, its gracious and mighty defender, since that place was consecrated to God, who visited it with manifold effect.

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Simon autem prædictus, pecuniarum et patriæ delator
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: But Simon, of whom we spoke before, who was the betrayer of the money, and of his country

paras.t: Recitatum est præcedenti capitulo, qualiter Deus virtuosum pontificem Oniam glorificavit. Hic describitur multiplex tribulatio atque injusta occisio ejus.
paras.en: It was related in the preceding chapter how God glorified the virtuous high priest Onias. Here are described his manifold tribulation and his unjust slaying.

paras.t: Simon autem prædictus, pecuniarum et patriæ delator, id est proditor, qui suos accusavit concives et proximos, prout in exordio præcedentis narratur capituli, male loquebatur habitatoribus Jerusalem de Onia, tanquam ipse Onias Heliodorum instigasset ad hæc, id est ad spoliandum ærarium; provisoremque civitatis, qui populo suo provisionem fecit de spiritualibus ac temporalibus bonis, ac defensorem gentis suæ Judaicæ, cujus pontifex fuit, quam et ab invisibilium hostium devoratione præservavit, ausus est insidiatorem regni dicere. Sic enim invidia mentem pervertit. Hunc impiissimum Simonem sequuntur iniqui, qui non solum se ipsos mendose excusant, sed alios quoque mendaciter criminantur, diffamant, et contra justos nituntur proximos inflammare.
paras.en: [[4:1|But Simon, of whom we spoke before, who was the betrayer of the money, and of his country|Simon autem prædictus, pecuniarum et patriæ delator]], that is, its traitor, who accused his own fellow citizens and neighbours, as is told at the beginning of the preceding chapter, [[4:1|spoke ill|male loquebatur]] to the inhabitants of Jerusalem [[4:1|of Onias, as though he had incited Heliodorus to do these things|de Onia, tanquam ipse Onias Heliodorum instigasset ad hæc]], that is, to plunder the treasury. [[4:2|And he presumed to call him a traitor to the kingdom|ausus est insidiatorem regni dicere]], him [[4:2|who provided for the city|provisoremque civitatis]], who made provision for his people of spiritual and temporal goods, [[4:2|and defended his nation|ac defensorem gentis suæ]], the Jewish nation, whose high priest he was, and which he also preserved from being devoured by invisible enemies. For so does envy pervert the mind. This most impious Simon is followed by the wicked, who not only excuse themselves falsely, but also lyingly accuse and defame others, and strive to inflame their neighbours against the just.

paras.t: Sed quum inimicitiæ Simonis contra Oniam in tantum procederent, ut etiam per quosdam Simonis necessarios, id est amicos, homicidia fierent, ita quod quosdam adhærentes Oniæ interfecerunt; considerans Onias periculum contentionis inter concives: nam et intestina bella maxime nocent; et Apollonium insanire, id est omnino irrationabiliter irasci et indignari Judæis, ad augendam malitiam Simonis, cui Apollonius iste favebat, ut patuit præcedenti capitulo; ad regem se contulit, id est, Seleucum accessit. Videbat enim, sine regali providentia impossibile esse, secundum viam humanam, pacem rebus, id est personis utriusque partis, dari: quas rex melius potuit cohibere. Reges quoque solent multos prudentes habere. Nec Simonem posse facili conatu cessare a stultitia sua, id est a stultis operibus quæ incepit. Erat enim habituatus in vitiis, atque pravissimæ consuetudinis mole victus.
paras.en: [[4:3|But when the enmities|Sed quum inimicitiæ]] of Simon against Onias [[4:3|proceeded so far|in tantum procederent]], [[4:3|that murders also were committed by some of Simon's friends|ut etiam per quosdam Simonis necessarios]] (*necessarii*, that is, intimates), so that they killed some of Onias's adherents: [[4:4|Onias, considering the danger of this contention|considerans Onias periculum contentionis]] among fellow citizens (for civil wars do the greatest harm), [[4:4|and that Apollonius|et Apollonium]] [[4:4|was outrageous|insanire]], that is, was wholly unreasonably angry and indignant with the Jews, [[4:4|which increased the malice of Simon|ad augendam malitiam Simonis]], whom this Apollonius favoured, as appeared in the preceding chapter, [[4:4|went to the king|ad regem se contulit]], that is, approached Seleucus. [[4:6|For he saw that, except the king took care, it was impossible|Videbat enim, sine regali providentia impossibile esse]], by human means, [[4:6|that matters should be settled in peace|pacem rebus]] (*matters*, that is, the persons of either party), whom the king was better able to restrain. Kings, too, are wont to have many prudent men about them. And he saw it was impossible [[4:6|that Simon would cease from his folly|Nec Simonem posse facili conatu cessare a stultitia sua]] by any easy effort, that is, from the foolish deeds he had begun. For he was habituated in vices, and overcome by the weight of a most depraved custom.

paras.t: Sed post Seleuci vitæ excessum, id est post mortem Seleuci regis, quum suscepisset regnum Antiochus, ambiebat Jason frater Oniæ summum sacerdotium: quod ab Antiocho Epiphane emere studuit. Cui et promittebat et alia centum quinquaginta talenta argenti, si potestati ejus concederetur ab Antiocho gymnasium, id est scholam gentilis ritus, et ephebiam sibi constituere, id est, prostibulum puerorum pulchrorum pro suo commodo facere: ephebus quippe vocatur puer formosus et lucidus; et eos qui in Jerosolymis erant, Antiochenos scribere, id est, in ritu gentilitatis esse et dici imitatores Antiochenorum.
paras.en: [[4:7|But after the death of Seleucus|Sed post Seleuci vitæ excessum]], that is, after the death of King Seleucus, [[4:7|when Antiochus, who was called the Illustrious, had taken possession of the kingdom|quum suscepisset regnum Antiochus]], [[4:7|Jason, the brother of Onias, ambitiously sought the high priesthood|ambiebat Jason frater Oniæ summum sacerdotium]], which he set about buying from Antiochus Epiphanes. To him he also promised [[4:9|a hundred and fifty more|et alia centum quinquaginta]] talents of silver, [[4:9|if he might have license|si potestati ejus concederetur]] from Antiochus [[4:9|to set him up a place for exercise|gymnasium]], that is, a school of the heathen rite, [[4:9|and a place for youth|et ephebiam sibi constituere]], that is, to make a brothel of handsome boys for his own pleasure: for a fair and bright boy is called *ephebus* [the *ephebeum* was in fact the hall of a gymnasium where youths were trained; Denis follows the medieval glosses]; [[4:9|and to entitle them that were at Jerusalem, Antiochians|et eos qui in Jerosolymis erant, Antiochenos scribere]], that is, that they should be of the heathen rite and be called imitators of the Antiochians.

paras.t: Quod quum rex annuisset, quia gentilis erat, et obtinuisset ipse Jason principatum sacerdotii, statim ad gentilem ritum contribules suos, id est Judæos suæ tribus, videlicet sacerdotes et sibi ex parte matris propinquos, transferre cœpit, ut sic ad paganismum induceret alios quoque Judæos. Et amotis his, id est ablatis a Judæis beneficiis ac privilegiis his, quæ humanitatis causa, id est ex pietate, Judæis a regibus Asiæ aut aliis fuerant constituta, id est data, per Joannem natione Judæum, qui ista procuravit a regibus, patrem Eupolemi: qui Eupolemius apud Romanos de amicitia et societate functus est legatione, id est, a Juda Machabæo missus est ad Romanos, ad constituendum cum illis amicitiam ac societatem, quemadmodum scriptum est in primo libro: Elegit Judas Eupolemium filium Joannis, et Jasonem filium Eleazari, et misit eos Romam; legitima civium jura destituens, id est, tollens ac dissipans divina præcepta ac legis divinæ statuta seu jura, prava instituta sanciebat, id est, vitiosas ordinationes ac jussiones instituit. Etenim ausus est sub ipsa arce, videlicet prope templum, gymnasium constituere, et optimos quosque epheborum, id est elegantiores pueros quos potuit adipisci, in lupanaribus ponere, ad exercendum in illis Sodomiticum crimen.
paras.en: [[4:10|Which when the king had granted|Quod quum rex annuisset]], because he was a heathen, [[4:10|and he had gotten the rule|et obtinuisset ipse Jason principatum]] of the priesthood, [[4:10|forthwith|statim]] [[4:10|he began to bring over his countrymen to the fashion of the heathens|ad gentilem ritum contribules suos]] (*countrymen*, that is, the Jews of his own tribe, namely the priests and his kin on his mother's side), so as thus to lead the other Jews too into paganism. [[4:11|And abolishing those things|Et amotis his]], that is, taking away from the Jews those benefits and privileges [[4:11|which had been decreed of special favour|quæ humanitatis causa]], that is, out of kindness, [[4:11|by the kings in behalf of the Jews|Judæis a regibus]] of Asia or others (*decreed*, that is, given), [[4:11|by the means of John|per Joannem]], a Jew by nation, who obtained these things from the kings, [[4:11|the father of that Eupolemus|patrem Eupolemi]], [[4:11|who went ambassador to Rome to make amity and alliance|qui Eupolemius apud Romanos de amicitia et societate functus est legatione]], that is, was sent by Judas Machabeus to the Romans to establish friendship and alliance with them, as is written in the first book: [[1 Mach 8:17|So Judas chose Eupolemus, the son of John|Elegit Judas Eupolemium filium Joannis]], [[1 Mach 8:17|and Jason, the son of Eleazar, and he sent them to Rome|et Jasonem filium Eleazari, et misit eos Romam]]; [[4:11|he disannulled the lawful ordinances of the citizens|legitima civium jura destituens]], that is, taking away and scattering the divine precepts and the statutes or laws of the divine law, [[4:11|and brought in fashions that were perverse|prava instituta sanciebat]], that is, he set up vicious ordinances and commands. [[4:12|For he had the boldness to set up, under the very castle|Etenim ausus est sub ipsa arce]], that is, near the temple, [[4:12|a place of exercise|gymnasium constituere]], [[4:12|and to put all the choicest youths|et optimos quosque epheborum]], that is, the more elegant boys he could get, [[4:12|in brothel houses|in lupanaribus ponere]], to practise the sin of Sodom with them.

paras.t: Erat autem hoc non initium, sed incrementum quoddam et profectus gentilis et alienigenæ conversationis. Vitium enim contra naturam non pertinet directe ad infidelitatem, sed carnalitatem turpissimam. Est tamen augmentum conversationis gentilis quæ veri Dei caret salutari notitia. Idcirco ad turpitudinem sine timore effundit se. Propter impii et non sacerdotis Jasonis nefarium et inauditum scelus, id est congeriem scelerum ejus. Jason autem indignissimus fuit nomine sacerdotis, nec fuit sacerdos Dei, exsecutione officii aut merito: nam et sacerdotes Dei ad idololatriam ac præfata gravissima traxit facinora. Ita ut sacerdotes jam non circa altaris officia dediti essent, sed festinarent participes fieri palæstræ, id est luctationis vel præfati gymnasii, et præbitionis ejus injustæ, id est vitiosæ exhibitionis institutionum Jasonis hujus, et in exercitiis disci, id est ludi quo discus seu plumbea scutella projiciebatur in aerem, et nunc vocatur ludus projiciendi lapides.
paras.en: [[4:13|Now this was not the beginning, but an increase, and progress of heathenish and foreign manners|Erat autem hoc non initium, sed incrementum quoddam et profectus gentilis et alienigenæ conversationis]]. For the vice against nature does not belong directly to unbelief, but to the foulest carnality. Yet it is an increase of the heathen way of life, which lacks the saving knowledge of the true God; and therefore it pours itself out into foulness without fear. And this came about [[4:13|through the abominable and unheard of wickedness of Jason, that impious wretch, and no priest|Propter impii et non sacerdotis Jasonis nefarium et inauditum scelus]] (*wickedness*, that is, the heap of his crimes). Jason was indeed most unworthy of the name of priest, nor was he a priest of God in the exercise of his office or in merit: for he dragged the priests of God too into idolatry and the most grievous crimes aforesaid. [[4:14|Insomuch that the priests were not now occupied about the offices of the altar|Ita ut sacerdotes jam non circa altaris officia dediti essent]], but [[4:14|hastened to be partakers of the games|festinarent participes fieri palæstræ]], that is, of the wrestling, or of the aforesaid place of exercise, [[4:14|and of the unlawful allowance thereof|et præbitionis ejus injustæ]], that is, of the vicious display of the institutions of this Jason, [[4:14|and of the exercise of the discus|et in exercitiis disci]], that is, of the game in which a discus or leaden dish was thrown into the air, which is now called the game of throwing stones.

paras.t: Et patrios quidem honores pro nihilo habentes, id est, venerandas observantias legis a patribus eorum servatas vilipendentes, Græcas glorias, id est actus et ritus Græcorum gentilium, in quibus ipsi Græci gloriabantur, optimas arbitrabantur. In quo gravissima patet excæcatio mentis eorum, quod tam stolidissime atque falsissime judicabant. Quarum gratia, id est propter quas glorias, periculosa eos contentio habebat, id est, intestinam dissensionem valde periculosam inciderunt: quia quibusdam idololatriæ illæ displicuerunt, aliis placuerunt; ac per omnia his consimiles in cultu idololatriæ gentilitatisque ritu esse cupiebant, quos hostes et peremptores habuerant, videlicet Syris et Græcis ac Asianis.
paras.en: [[4:15|And setting nought by the honours of their fathers|Et patrios quidem honores pro nihilo habentes]], that is, despising the venerable observances of the law kept by their fathers, [[4:15|they esteemed the Grecian glories|Græcas glorias]], that is, the acts and rites of the heathen Greeks, in which the Greeks themselves gloried, [[4:15|for the best|optimas arbitrabantur]]. In this the most grievous blindness of their mind is plain, that they judged so very stupidly and falsely. [[4:16|For the sake of which|Quarum gratia]], that is, for the sake of which glories, [[4:16|they incurred a dangerous contention|periculosa eos contentio habebat]], that is, they fell into a very dangerous civil dissension, because those idolatries displeased some and pleased others; [[4:16|and in all things they coveted to be like them|ac per omnia his consimiles]] in the worship of idols and the rite of heathendom, [[4:16|who were their enemies and murderers|quos hostes et peremptores habuerant]], namely the Syrians, the Greeks and the Asians.

paras.t: In leges enim divinas impie agere, eas transgrediendo, impune non cedit: juxta illud Psalmistæ: Maledicti qui declinant a mandatis tuis; Job quoque: Deus inultum abire non patitur. Sed hoc sequens tempus declarabit, id est, veritas horum patebit ex sequentibus, in quibus et ea narrantur, quæ contigerunt post tempus illud in quo contigerunt prædicta. Tempori autem adscribuntur ea quæ fiunt in tempore.
paras.en: [[4:17|For acting wickedly against the laws of God|In leges enim divinas impie agere]], by transgressing them, [[4:17|doth not pass unpunished|impune non cedit]]: according to that saying of the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:21|they are cursed who decline from thy commandments|Maledicti qui declinant a mandatis tuis]]; and Job too: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]]. But [[4:17|this the time following will declare|hoc sequens tempus declarabit]], that is, the truth of these things will appear from what follows, in which are also told the things that happened after the time in which the aforesaid happened. For the things that happen in time are ascribed to time.

paras.t: Quum autem quinquennalis agon, id est lucta seu concertatio exercitativa, quæ de quinquennio in quinquennium fiebat, Tyri celebraretur, id est, in loco illo solenniter fieret, et rex, scilicet Antiochus Nobilis, præsens esset. Fiebat enim lucta illa ad reverentiam Herculis, qui pugnator fuit fortissimus. Misit Jason viros portantes argenti didrachmas trecentas in sacrificium Herculis: quas postulaverunt hi qui asportaverunt, id est eas secum tulerunt, ne in sacrificiis Herculis erogarentur, quia non oporteret, id est, nec necessarium, imo nec utile esset. Propter præsentes autem, id est ad instantiam eorum qui aderant, datæ sunt in fabricam navium triremium, id est ad construendum naves in quibus erant ordines tres remorum.
paras.en: [[4:18|Now when the game that was used every fifth year|Quum autem quinquennalis agon]], that is, the wrestling or contest of exercise that was held every five years, [[4:18|was kept at Tyre|Tyri celebraretur]], that is, was solemnly held in that place, [[4:18|the king|et rex]], namely Antiochus the Illustrious, [[4:18|being present|præsens esset]]. For that contest was held in honour of Hercules, who was a most mighty fighter.
